 By  The Canadian Press 
 TOKYO - Canada’s Leylah Fernandez defeated fifth-seeded Elise Mertens of Belgium 6-2, 7-6 (8) in second-round women’s singles tennis action at the Japan Open.
 Fernandez, of Laval, Que., went ahead 4-1 in the second set before Mertens staged her comeback effort Thursday morning in Tokyo.
 After dropping the next two games, Fernandez made it 5-3, but again gave up two consecutive games.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 In the tiebreak, Mertens won the first three points before Fernandez answered with three straight of her own. 
 A back-and-forth affair eventually led to Mertens taking an 8-7 edge but Fernandez won the last three points to seal the victory.
 Fernandez had three double faults and went without an ace. However, she converted four of her 11 break-point opportunities.
 This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 28, 2026.
